chapter: Later career and The Benny Goodman Story
title: Recent work: Colorado Springs, Boston, Cleveland and the Ingrid Bergman tribute
summary: At the start of the January 1980 session Wilson lists recent engagements and playing 'As Time Goes By' on CBS with Sinatra.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: This is January 3rd, 1980, and here we are again with my dear friend, Teddy Wilson. Teddy, I think it was September 2nd the last time we talked, and you and I have both been running around the country since then and hadn't been able to get togeher.
When did we talk last, Colorado Springs, wasn't it?

Colorado Springs, yes, Dick Gibson's annual jazz party. Of course, in that period, and up until recently, I've been steadily engaged by this Copley Plaza Hotel here in New York playing the Plaza Bar --

Yes, Boston. And let's see, I've been doing a few outside things beside the Plaza bar, let me see, after Colorado Springs, I went to Cleveland, in October -- there was a date in Cleveland, and my two boys Theodore played bass with me, and Steven played drums, but a private jazz party, it was at the Madda Mansion, put on by a man named Ridley Watts who's quite a sponsor of jazz in Cleveland, ad has these special jazz parties, very similar to Dick Gibson's parties in Colorado Springs.
And I think that's about the -- oh, and I went out to Hollywood late in November to work on the tribute to Ingrid Bergman.
Right. They recreated many of her

movies in this tribute to Ingrid Bergman, and this recreation American of the Casablanca scene in Rick's Cafe, you know, where Humphrey Bogart had that little club, and they got me to play the piano, because the original pianist in the movie, the actor, Dooley Wilson, had passed away --

And so they have a scene where I ask Ingrid Bergman if she can still hum the tune like she did in the movie, and she starts humming 'As Time Goes By,' and then I start playing it on the piano, and in the door walks unannounced and a complete surprise to Ingrid Bergman -- Frank Sinatra singing the song, 'As Time Goes By.' As part of the general tribute to Ingrid Bergman, and that was shown on December 6th on the CBS network.
And I think that's about all the special work I've done since I've seen you, Milt. Otherwise, it's just been the Plaza Bar work.

Well, that's beautiful. The first time -- to continue, we were talking about some of the nice things that Dick Hyman had done for you because of the nice things you did for him when he was a young man and how much he appreciated it.
